data.title: Proposed Immigration Rules: 60-Day Grace Period & Visa Extensions
data.summary: If you are a foreign professional working in the United States on a temporary visa, two proposed changes can affect your short- and long-term plans. One would change what happens when a job ends. The other would change how USCIS reviews requests to extend a previously approved petition. [...] These are two separate regulatory proposals, and neither has been finalized. The existing regulations remain in effect unless and until new regulations become legally effective. Nevertheless, if implemented, these proposed changes could significantly affect foreign workers’ career decisions and long-term immigration planning. data.title: 80% pay cut or leave by December 31: Why IBM’s US visa sponsorship freeze puts Indian tech workers in a tough spot | Us-news News - The Indian Express
data.summary: In September 2025, the Trump administration had also announced a $100,000 fee on certain fresh H-1B petitions involving workers entering the US from overseas. The levy has since faced legal challenges. Separately, the US has replaced its traditional H-1B visa lottery with a weighted selection system that accords greater preference to higher-paid workers, a move with implications for Indian IT services companies, which have historically been among the largest users of the visa programme. [...] Stay updated with the latest - Click here to follow us on Instagram American technology major IBM has decided to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of foreign workers in its consulting business in the US, asking affected employees to either relocate to another country or leave the company by the end of this year. [...] There has been a sharp decline in H-1B registrations amid these changes. According to US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) data, the number of eligible registrations for cap-subject H-1B visas fell by 38.5% to around 211,600 for the 2027 financial year, compared with 343,981 a year earlier.

data.title: IBM Tells H-1B Visa Holders To Leave US Or Quit. What It Means For Indians
data.summary: US Visa Rules Add To Uncertainty For Indian Tech Workers IBM's decision comes at a time when the US administration has increased scrutiny of employment-based immigration programmes. The H-1B visa programme allows American companies to hire foreign professionals for specialised jobs. Indian technology workers have been among its biggest beneficiaries. [...] However, the Trump administration has moved to make the programme more restrictive. Its measures include a proposed $100,000 fee for certain new H-1B petitions and changes to the visa selection process that give greater weight to higher-paid positions. The administration has also stepped up action against companies over alleged misuse of employment-based immigration programmes. [...] According to media reports, employees have been given three weeks to decide whether they want to relocate. Those who do not accept an overseas position will be offered three months' severance, with December 31, 2026, set as their last working day. Why Has IBM Decided To Stop Visa Sponsorship? IBM has attributed the decision to changing business requirements and the availability of skilled workers.

data.title: IBM ends US visa sponsorship, gives H-1B workers three weeks to relocate or leave company
data.summary: What IBM says about ending visa sponsorship IBM has attributed the decision to changes in the availability of skilled workers and the requirements of its clients. "IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages," an IBM spokesperson told Rest of World. The spokesperson added that the company's participation in these programmes had been declining for several years. [...] In September 2025, the White House announced a one-time USD 100,000 fee on certain new H-1B visa applications. The measure has since faced legal challenges. The administration has also proposed changes to the annual H-1B selection process that would give greater weight to higher-paid applicants. More recently, the US Department of Labor suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several major IT outsourcing companies from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) process, according to Reuters. [...] The decision also comes against the backdrop of a decline in IBM's H-1B petition approvals. Federal immigration records show that the company received just over 1,600 approvals in fiscal year 2026, compared with more than 2,000 in FY2025 and nearly 3,000 in FY2024. US immigration restrictions add to uncertainty IBM's move comes as technology companies navigate tighter scrutiny of foreign-worker hiring under President Donald Trump's administration.
